title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
content: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
content: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
content: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.

title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
content: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

title: The Price of You
content: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

title: Investing in Brain Health
content: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
content: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.

title: Energy Security in an Age of Disruption
content: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives.

title: Africa’s Common Currency-in-Waiting
content: While the phased approach of the Economic Community of West African States to implementing a long-delayed single currency will maintain momentum without compromising macroeconomic discipline, the bloc still lacks a robust mechanism to address asymmetric shocks. That is why fiscal integration must come first.

content: Political discourse in many Western countries has broken down, making it difficult for people with different viewpoints to live amicably with one another. The Reconciliation League, an international initiative by 13 universities and colleges, aims to train a generation of leaders who can change that.

content: After two years in office, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum continues to be widely praised, both in Mexico and abroad, for her handling of US President Donald Trump. But Sheinbaum has skillfully—and cynically—disguised the extent to which she has deferred to Trump on almost every issue.

title: Distorted Intelligence at the AI Frontier
content: The real problem for the frontier AI labs is not that their models are too powerful and already “misaligned” with the goals their creators set for them. Rather, it is that the models are being trained in ways that may be leading to a type of intelligence that will become less predictable.

content: Although the Labour Party has done more to strengthen the United Kingdom's public-finance ecosystem in the past two years than any government in a generation, it must not stop there. If public investment is to meet its full potential, it must be reorganized to operate at scale on the public's behalf.

title: An EU–Canada Partnership Against Coercion
content: By proposing that the European Union and Canada begin work toward an association agreement, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has taken a critical first step toward establishing Europe as a hub for the world’s democratic middle powers. Such an arrangement would enable resistance to US pressure without decoupling from the US.

title: The Opposing Forces Reshaping Global Finance
content: The financial industry is being pulled between two powerful forces: bottom-up financial technology is enabling seamless integration, while top-down geoeconomic statecraft is promoting fragmentation. So much for the conventional wisdom that finance will simply become smoother, cheaper, and more globalized over time.

title: Oligarchy Is a Symptom, Not a Cause
content: The deepening political dysfunction plaguing the US can be traced not to wealth inequality, as some argue, but to the fact that different groups of voters believe different facts. A political strategy that takes this into account might eventually lead to wealth redistribution, but it must begin with improved critical-thinking skills.

content: Right-wing populists have turned hypocrisy into a successful electoral strategy. But those voting for nativism in Europe and the United States should be careful what they wish for: They may end up expelling their own family members, if not their own political leaders.

content: As the two world leaders in AI development and adoption, the United States and China are each operating under assumptions that justify ever-faster progress, regardless of the risks. The current thinking is not unlike the rationale once given for Stalinist brutality in the name of rapid modernization.

title: The Un-Ordered UN Order
content: As European leaders hobnob with their counterparts at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, they must think carefully about how to navigate a fast-changing multilateral landscape. The old world belonged to rule-makers and institution-builders, but the current one favors those who can improvise.

title: AI Needs Trusted Journalism
content: As people increasingly rely on AI chatbots for news, the already tenuous bargain between publishers and tech firms—the former invested in journalism that the latter helped audiences discover—is no longer workable. UNESCO’s proposed Guidance on Fair Compensation for News could help create a new value-exchange model.

content: Until this month, a far-right, openly ethnonationalist party had never come so close to winning an absolute majority in an election in the Federal Republic of Germany. Now that it has, and with similarly pro-Russian forces on the rise in France, all Europeans must prepare for the worst.

title: UN Peacekeeping in Crisis
content: With the world facing the largest number of armed conflicts since 1946, the Trump administration’s continuing assault on the United Nations has prevented the organization from fulfilling its peacekeeping duties. A recent report by UN Secretary-General António Guterres shows how the organization has few, if any, levers to fight back.

title: The Dismally Obedient Science
content: While empirical inquiry has its place in economics, the pursuit of causality must not be allowed to displace the pursuit of explanation. Beyond identifying causal effects within existing arrangements, economists must investigate how those arrangements are produced, reproduced, and contested.
